hypothesis: Frank-relevant semantic retrieval can become materially faster and more correct by keeping UnifiedDB as semantic authority while using epoch/provenance-bound ClayGraph materializations for bounded hot reads.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Any gain is only ordinary indexing; a well-indexed normal relational database with the same semantics will match Clay, and derived heads may silently change latest/tombstone semantics.

unifieddb_query_plane.adjudication: SUPPORTED: bounded SQL pushdown preserves sampled semantics and removes full-state decode from the hot read. Concurrent worker implementation commit 8d5beaa28969c553735edfe91a09ec3e56f0c0fe matches the measured direction.

strong_generic_relational_baseline.description: SQLite with sensible CURRENT partial indexes and ordinary source/target indexes, but without Clay-specific semantic policy/projections.
strong_generic_relational_baseline.adjudication: COUNTERHYPOTHESIS PARTLY SUPPORTED: Clay is not intrinsically more accurate than a normal DB engine given identical semantic structure and ranking policy. Accuracy gain must come from semantics/provenance/projections, not branding or storage engine.

synthetic_ambiguous_retrieval.adjudication: SUPPORTED ONLY FOR SYNTHETIC AMBIGUITY WORKLOAD; requires Frank-held-out/live validation before promotion.

claygraph_v3_semantic_access_falsifier.v3_bug: v_current_graph_semantic_access_paths computes MAX(graph_epoch) only over status=CURRENT, so a newer QUARANTINED/SUPERSEDED version can revive an older CURRENT path.
claygraph_v3_semantic_access_falsifier.strict_reference_semantics: select newest version per (seed,target) regardless status, then expose only if newest status=CURRENT
claygraph_v3_semantic_access_falsifier.adjudication: SUPPORTED CANDIDATE: strict heads remove observed stale resurrection and recover the performance cost of correct latest-version semantics. Promotion still requires exact repository tests, ambiguity gate, rebuild equivalence and target/Ubuntu replication.

web_fusion.finding: Partial/multicolumn/covering indexes are standard database mechanisms. Clay's defensible differentiation is coherent epoch/provenance/admissibility semantics plus workload-specific rebuildable projections, not generic index existence.

architecture_delta.rollback: Do not admit V4; continue V3 views. V4 adds only derived/rebuildable acceleration and strict candidate views until verified receipt exists.

negative_results: Universal claim that Clay is more accurate merely because it is Clay: REFUTED.
WITHOUT ROWID/capsule shortcut as a meaningful architecture improvement on measured workload: NO_BENEFIT.
Global latest-epoch shortcut as sufficient semantics under partial rebuild: REJECTED; strict per-key latest semantics required.
next_falsifiers: Run repository V4 anti-resurrection tests on an exact checkout.
Full-row strict-vs-fast equivalence over real ClayGraph corpus with ambiguity_count=0.

Ubuntu/Hostinger replication through an actually authorized compatible lane.
